title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Payment Channels, Fees and Refund Terms
content:
The terms below govern voluntary repayments toward Benefit Overpayment Accounts and are the same for all six classifications: Non-Fraud Overpayment — Agency Error, Non-Fraud Overpayment — Employer Reporting Error, Non-Fraud Overpayment — Appeal Reversal, Non-Fraud Overpayment — Claimant Error, Fraud Overpayment — First Offense and Fraud Overpayment — Repeat Offense.

| Term | Figure for every classification |
|---|---|
| Channels through which voluntary repayments are accepted | Online bank debit (ACH), debit or credit card, check, money order |
| Vendor convenience fee on card repayments | 0.0235 of the repayment (2.35 percent), paid on top of the repayment and never applied to the balance |
| Returned-payment fee schedule figure | USD 25.00 |
| Smallest excess repayment refunded to the claimant | USD 1.00 |
| Business days to issue a refund of excess repayments or of recoveries on a cancelled overpayment | 10 |
| Voluntary repayments accepted while recovery is suspended for an appeal or a waiver review | Yes |
| Balance statements while a balance is open | Mailed monthly |

## Terms in plain words

- The **convenience fee** is the card vendor's own charge. It is paid by the claimant in addition to the repayment, and it never reduces the overpayment balance.
- The **returned-payment fee** figure is the classification's fee for a repayment that the bank returns unpaid.
- An **excess repayment** is money recovered beyond what is owed on the overpayment. The minimum refund figure is the smallest excess that is refunded.

## Illustration on hypothetical amounts

*Hypothetical:* a claimant pays USD 200.00 toward a balance by card. The vendor's convenience fee is 2.35 percent of USD 200.00, USD 4.70, paid on top. The balance falls by USD 200.00, not by USD 204.70.
